brief.title: Draft checks for a verb's output
brief.plain_summary: From the template that shapes a verb's output, write deterministic checks and rubric items that would catch the failures that matter.
brief.outcome: A private check suite, or no_change when an existing suite already covers the template.

output_template.description: Pin of the template noun that defines the output shape. Any template category works; use the nearest one.

failure_records.description: Pins of known failures of this output, if any.

template_id.description: The verb template whose output these checks guard.

output_store.description: Store for the produced private nouns. The default is a placeholder; use the store your owner assigned.

output_contract.delivery: Private nouns are readable only by the key that wrote them. Include each produced value in output.artifacts[].value with its pin so the requester can verify it through the task result. Never widen visibility or allowlist other surfaces.

outcome_meanings.suite_ready: The declared nouns were produced and every deterministic acceptance check passed.
outcome_meanings.no_change: The evidence does not justify producing or changing anything. Say why.
outcome_meanings.unknown: The question could not be answered with the permitted inputs. List what is missing and what would resolve it.
outcome_meanings.blocked: A required input, permission or capability is missing. Ask one precise question.

acceptance_checks.check: The suite validates against template.check-suite's schema.
Every deterministic rule uses only rule types listed in rule-types.
Every rule stated in the output template has at least one check.

required: Verify the pins and read the output template's schema and rules.
Write a deterministic rule wherever the property can be decided from the document alone.
Write a rubric item only for properties that need judgment, and say what a good and a bad answer look like.
Give every check a reason a reader can verify.

execution.inference_allowance: Existing authorized worker allowance only. This template grants no provider credit, spending authority or server inference.

instantiation.rule: Replace each slot with exact NounRef pins, set the params, then recompute the idempotency key with scripts/build_packs.py --instantiate. Enqueue only with your own grants in a queue your owner assigned.

execution_report.purpose: Lets later runs of this template be fingerprinted and compared. It is worker reported, not proof.

summaries.problem: One sentence: what this run was asked to resolve.
summaries.input: One sentence: which pinned inputs were read.
summaries.solution: One sentence: what was produced or why the outcome was no_change, unknown or blocked.

usage.reason: Template only. Replace with measured counters or keep null with a reason.

fill_rules: Copy contract.input_schema and contract.output_schema unchanged, so every run of this template shares one shape fingerprint.
Add context_hash, environment_hash and toolchain_hash as lowercase SHA-256 digests when known; all five contract fields together allow exact matching.
Name the exact harness version, provider and model. Deterministic or human work records the model name as none.
Put what went wrong in an error block and in output.run_notes.went_wrong. The version-1 report has no fields for what went right, next steps or ideas, so those go in output.run_notes.
Leave token counts null with a reason unless the harness or provider measured them.

dimension_basis.reason: Tessera requires these axes, so each is set to its lowest value and the tier is unverified. No quality is claimed. Replace them only with measured values and the evidence that produced them.

brief.title: Build known-good and known-bad examples
brief.plain_summary: Collect known-good outputs and real failures, then add targeted mutations so every check has something it should catch.
brief.outcome: A private example set with provenance for every example.

check_suite.description: Pin of the check suite to exercise.

accepted_outputs.description: Pins of accepted outputs to use as known-good examples.

failure_records.description: Pins of real failures to use as known-bad examples.

acceptance_checks.check: The example set validates against template.example-set's schema.
Every deterministic check id appears in some mutation's targets.
Every mutation uses an operator listed in mutation-operators.
Known-bad examples resemble failures that actually happen.

required: Confirm you did not draft this check suite; otherwise return blocked.
Use accepted outputs with receipts as known-good where possible; sanitize anything private.
Add at least one targeted mutation for every deterministic check, using only the listed operators.
Never edit a known-good example to suit a check.

brief.title: Validate the checks
brief.plain_summary: Run every deterministic check against every known-good example, known-bad example and mutation, twice, and apply the trust rule.
brief.outcome: A private check validation with a trusted, revise or reject verdict per check.

acceptance_checks.check: The validation validates against template.check-validation's schema.
The worked example's expected summary, caught map and verdicts were reproduced exactly.
Every verdict equals the trust rule applied to its summary row.
The second pass gave identical results.

required: Reproduce the pinned worked example's expected results first; stop with blocked if they differ.
Apply each mutation to its known-good examples with the listed operators only.
Run every check on every example and mutant; run the whole pass a second time and compare.
Apply the trust rule exactly. Report targeted mutations a check missed.
